The league season had [[Club Atlético Vélez Sársfield|Vélez Sársfield]] winning both, Apertura and Clausura championships (3rd. and 4th. league titles for the club). [[Estudiantes de La Plata]] (as champion of [[1994–95 Primera B Nacional]]) and [[Club Atlético Colón|Colón de Santa Fe]] (winner of "Torneo Octogonal" after beating [[San Martín de Tucumán]] in a two-legged series)[https://www.ellitoral.com/index.php/id_um/203517-se-cumplen-24-anos-del-ascenso-de-colon-29-de-julio-de-1995-actualidad-sabalera.html Se cumplen 24 años del ascenso de Colón], El Litoral, 29 Jul 2019 promoted from the [[Primera B Nacional]] (second division).[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/arg96.html Argentina 1995/96] by Pablo Ciullini on the RSSSF On the other hand, [[Club Atlético Belgrano|Belgrano (Córdoba)]] and [[Argentinos Juniors]] were relegated to Primera B Nacional."Argentina: 1ra. División AFA - Torneo Clausura 1996" by José Carluccio on Historia y Futbol (blogsite), 12 June 2012 The 1994 Apertura was the first season in which the league implemented a system awarding 3 points per match won, after [[FIFA]] had ruled it worldwide.[https://elpais.com/diario/1994/10/29/deportes/783385203_850215.html La FIFA obliga a todas las ligas a conceder tres puntos por victoria], El
